text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two new documents have been given to the Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders meeting in Montreux, Switzerland on procedural issues and issues of substance relating to the talks. Both sides have to issue their responses to U.N. envoy Diego Cordovez today.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash claims progress in Montreux talks, vowing to stay until the end of the five-day meeting.
- Cyprus lodges an official protest at the United Nations over an agreement signed last week on the partial integration of Turkey and northern Cyprus.

- Cyprus Telecommunications Authority Cyta invites bids from stockbrokers for the execution and management of a 26 million pound ($47.5 million) portfolio the authority intends to invest in government bonds.
- Local dairy Christis signs a deal with Denmark-based Nordex Food A/S whereby the Danes will cease manufacturing the Cypriot Halloumi cheese and contract Christis to make it.
- New Cordovez documents are put on the table at Montreux. "Times are difficult," says President Glafcos Clerides.
- Unions at Limassol port threaten to go on strike if the port authority goes ahead and dismisses port workers.
- New Cordovez documents are tabled on key aspects of the Cyprus dispute and procedural issues.
